# Intent

## What is being built

Open-source packet analyzer. The CLI takes tshark's flags and filters. A field query reads only the bytes that field needs, so it runs near the speed of memory or disk instead of the speed of tshark's per-packet engine. The same reader indexes capture archives, exports Parquet, and drives a desktop app that replaces Wireshark.

## For whom

Network engineers and security analysts who already use Wireshark and tshark.

## Disciplines

software

## Constraints

none recorded

## Team

solo

## Values

Correctness.

## Taste

Short files.

## Process weight

Low

## Always-on

### own-the-harness

When: you work in this product repo

You run ax. Do not ask the human to run commands.

People talk. You save. The next chat already knows.

AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md stay short: the vision, the few rules that must always be on, and one sentence per decision still in force. The sentence is the decision. The path beside it is the file. Open that file only when you need more than the sentence. Do not open every decision file. Do not log a decision for something the vision already says, or for a task you are about to do. Do not edit AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md by hand.

Edit `.ax/intent.md` for the vision, then run `ax compile`. Log the rest with these commands. Each one rewrites the root files before it returns. Do not ask the human to compile.

- `ax log decision "<title>"` reads markdown on stdin: `## Context`, `## Options`, `## Choice`, `## Why`. ## Choice is one sentence. No pipe writes those headings empty.
- `ax log observation "<finding>" --method "<how>"`
- `ax log friction "<one line>"`

Offer the rest in chat. They say yes or no:

- A check failed: say so.
- They want a rule to stick: write the decision and a check that points at it.
- The same pain repeats: suggest a rule, or a short scored task.
- A reminder looks outdated: ask to drop it.
- The next project should work the same way: copy the useful part.
- A new editor: compile that target. The `.ax` record does not move.
- Another machine: run `ax doctor` without being asked. Say what is wrong.
- Newer ax: say what would change. They say yes or no.

Leave a retro proposal unmerged until they accept it.

## Decisions in force

- Adopt ax. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-09-adopt-ax-for-harness-management.md`)
- The first work is a tshark behavior study and performance baseline, before any decoder. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-09-measure-tshark-before-any-decoder.md`)
- fin's speed comes from a query-specific reader, and the headline number is TLS server-name extraction against tshark. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-09-quote-tls-server-names-as-the-speed-claim.md`)
- Process weight is Low for a solo team. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-09-record-a-solo-team.md`)
- Disciplines are software and constraints are none recorded. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-09-record-software-as-the-discipline.md`)
- The packet analyzer is implemented in Rust. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-09-write-the-analyzer-in-rust.md`)
- The v1 reader compiles one plan, matches tshark 4.6.9 on claimed paths, and counts any frame it cannot prove. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-10-close-the-uncounted-tshark-gaps.md`)
- Commit messages use Conventional Commits: a type, an optional scope, and an imperative subject. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-10-use-conventional-commit-messages.md`)
- Pcapng options follow tshark 4.6.9 pcapng.c, and a fault exits 3 before any packet block and 14 after. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-11-pcapng-options-match-tshark-4-6-9.md`)
- CI installs tshark 4.6.9 from the official SHA256-pinned source tarball; local oracle tests skip if that binary is missing. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-11-pin-tshark-4-6-9-in-ci.md`)
- v1 frames are link type and captured bytes; parse timestamps and original length when a query needs them. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-11-v1-frames-drop-unused-time.md`)
- A non-empty UDP or TCP payload is proved when the winning port dissector always claims and does not reach IP, except VXLAN which is walked; otherwise the frame is counted. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-13-claim-a-udp-or-tcp-payload-only-when.md`)
- Stderr prints every counted line with frame and reason, then a total, and the process exits nonzero when any frame was counted. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-13-print-every-counted-frame-on-stderr.md`)
- Build the diff harness, then the sequential reader, then ip.src including VXLAN, then the chunk split, then TLS server names, then HTTP. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-13-put-vxlan-in-ip-src-and-http-after-tls.md`)
- A throwing handshake message aborts later handshake messages in that TLS record, keeping SNI from ClientHellos before the throw. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-abort-later-handshake-messages-after-a-throw.md`)
- A CertificateURL whose tshark 4.6.9 ssl_dissect_hnd_cert_url throws aborts leftover, matching dissect_ssl. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-abort-payload-after-a-throwing-certificateurl.md`)
- A heartbeat whose tshark 4.6.9 dissector throws aborts the rest of that payload, matching dissect_ssl. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-abort-payload-after-a-throwing-heartbeat.md`)
- Print ClientHello SNI on the frame that completed that hello, and buffer only the truncated handshake record as tshark 4.6.9 desegment_offset does. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-buffer-only-the-truncated-tls-handshake.md`)
- CCS uses client_ccs_frame and server_ccs_frame on the TCP conversation; ssl_packet_from_server starts from the TLS port table and flips when ClientHello calls ssl_set_server(dst). (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-ccs-follows-ssl-packet-from-server.md`)
- Desegment any incomplete TLS record, not only handshake, matching tshark 4.6.9 dissect_ssl3_record. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-desegment-any-incomplete-tls-record.md`)
- Desegment an incomplete TLS record even when its u16 length is 18432–65535, matching tshark 4.6.9 dissect_ssl3_record. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-desegment-incomplete-tls-records-above-tls-max-record.md`)
- A claimed TLS conversation desegments leftover shorter than a record header even when the session is unknown and leftover is not a content type. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-desegment-leftover-shorter-than-a-tls-record-header.md`)
- A truncated handshake after a complete CCS, alert, app-data, or HelloRequest is buffered like tshark 4.6.9 dissect_ssl, and the completing segment prints SNI. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-desegment-truncated-handshake-after-a-complete-tls-record.md`)
- A length-0 CCS still sets ccs_frame when tshark 4.6.9 tvb_get_uint8 for next_byte succeeds. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-empty-ccs-leftover-sets-ccs-frame.md`)
- A length-0 handshake stays Unproved, but ssl_try_set_version reads next_byte as the handshake type so a following CCS can stick. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-empty-handshake-next-byte-sticks-the-tls-session.md`)
- A new TLS handshake record of 16 or more bytes is encrypted when tshark 4.6.9 is_encrypted_handshake_message is true. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-follow-tshark-encrypted-handshake.md`)
- A complete handshake whose tshark 4.6.9 dissector throws leaves leftover unprocessed, so the next ClientHello is a new record. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-handshake-throw-leaves-leftover-unprocessed.md`)
- A heartbeat whose tshark 4.6.9 dissector throws leaves leftover unprocessed, matching dissect_ssl3_heartbeat. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-heartbeat-throw-leaves-leftover-unprocessed.md`)
- A complete TLS record with an incomplete handshake still desegments; the next in-order payload on that flow is continuation, matching tshark 4.6.9 dissect_tls_handshake. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-incomplete-handshake-desegments-like-tshark.md`)
- A length-0 CCS, alert, app-data, or heartbeat sticks the TLS session only when a later byte in the same payload is readable. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-length-0-tls-records-do-not-stick-the-session.md`)
- A valid non-ClientHello TLS handshake with SSLv3/TLS 1.0–1.2/TLCP sticks the session the way tshark 4.6.9 ssl_try_set_version does. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-non-clienthello-handshake-sticks-tls-version.md`)
- Skip a length-0 CCS, alert, app-data, or heartbeat record and keep walking, matching tshark 4.6.9 dissect_ssl. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-skip-empty-non-handshake-tls-records.md`)
- Skip length-0 TLS records when looking for a truncated handshake, matching tshark 4.6.9 dissect_ssl. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-skip-empty-tls-records-when-desegmenting.md`)
- ssl_set_server(dst) runs when dissect_ssl enters the ClientHello arm, including an empty or short hello. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-ssl-set-server-on-clienthello-entry.md`)
- A ServerHello supported_versions of TLS 1.3 sets the session like tshark 4.6.9 ssl_try_set_version, so later records need ssl_looks_like_sslv3. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-tls-1-3-serverhello-unsticks-grease-records.md`)
- Unnamed ports use is_sslv3_or_tls; a TLS port uses ssl_looks_like_sslv3 until an authoritative SSLv3/TLS 1.0–1.2/TLCP record, then dissect_ssl3_record. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-tls-heuristic-vs-named-port-record-rules.md`)
- ssl_packet_from_server looks up the snapshotted tls.port table, not first-named tls on tcp.port. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-tls-port-is-ssl-associations.md`)
- SslSession.version is unknown, a sticky pre-1.3 version, or TLS 1.3, so a later 0x0303 record cannot unstick TLS 1.3. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-tls-session-version-is-unknown-sticky-or-1-3.md`)
- tls_known and tls_claimed are keyed by the TCP conversation, both directions, matching tshark 4.6.9 SslSession. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-21-tls-version-sticks-on-the-tcp-conversation.md`)
- compress_certificate throws on an odd 2-byte algorithm-ID hello-tvb read, QUIC transport_parameters on a type/length varint overrun, and ESNI only when rem < 4. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-27-clienthello-compress-certificate-quic-tp-and-esni-throw-bounds.md`)
- Count a last ClientHello extension whose tshark 4.6.9 throw fin cannot prove, and keep only exact fixed-width hello-tvb reads. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-27-count-unclear-last-clienthello-extensions.md`)
- Last-ext ALPN, status_request_v2, oid_filters, and trusted_ca_keys throw on a hello-tvb overrun, and a QUIC TP length varint wraps to u32. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-27-last-ext-alpn-status-request-v2-oid-filters-trusted-ca-keys-throw-quic-tp.md`)
- Match tshark 4.6.9 last-ext throws for pre_shared_key, certificate_authorities, trusted_ca_keys x509_name, and oid_filters values; ALPN ja4 is first-name only; status_request_v2 walks OCSP. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-27-last-ext-psk-cert-authorities-and-refined-alpn-ocsp-ber-throws.md`)
- QUIC transport_parameters throw when a known parameter's proto_tree_add_item or ENC_VARINT_QUIC read overruns the hello tvb, even if parameter_length is 0. (`.ax/decisions/2026-10-27-quic-tp-parameter-type-hello-tvb-reads-throw.md`)
- After CONNECT plus 2xx, later Hosts are counted http-tunnel unless the URI port's tcp.port name is http or tls. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-connect-2xx-tunnels-unless-uri-port-is-http.md`)
- An incomplete HTTP message marks that TCP direction so a later payload there is counted continuation, not a new Host. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-count-desegment-body-continuation-instead-of-printing-host.md`)
- After SSTP_DUPLEX_POST plus 200 or a 101 with Upgrade, later Hosts on that conversation are counted as an unwalked tunnel. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-count-host-after-sstp-and-101-upgrade-as-an.md`)
- Leftover TLVs after a jumbo 4-byte read in the same hop/dest header are counted; jumbo that fills the header still walks next. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-count-leftover-hop-dest-tlvs-after-jumbo.md`)
- A non-plain HTTP TCP segment is counted; a gap or contained retransmission stays blank; SYN and RST still set nxtseq to seq+1. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-count-non-plain-http-tcp-segments.md`)
- Leftover bytes in the same TCP segment after a complete 101 with Upgrade or SSTP_DUPLEX_POST plus 200 are counted as an unwalked tunnel. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-count-same-segment-leftover-after-101-sstp-as-a-tunnel.md`)
- An empty-payload TCP SYN still sets that direction's HTTP nxtseq to seq+1. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-empty-syn-still-sets-http-nxtseq-to-seq-1.md`)
- Fin does not implement --version; tshark 4.6.9 is the oracle, recorded in the harness pin and README. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-fin-does-not-implement-version.md`)
- An HTTP/2 preface is leftover after the Content-Length body, not the body bytes themselves. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-http-2-magic-in-a-content-length-body-is-not.md`)
- HTTP/2 on a named http port is counted, not proved. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-http-2-on-a-named-http-port-is-counted.md`)
- A 1xx does not clear a pending SSTP_DUPLEX_POST, so a later 200 still switches leftover Hosts to an unwalked tunnel. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-keep-sstp-pending-through-a-1xx.md`)
- A one-segment HTTP/1.x message on a snapshotted http TCP port prints http.host; split, TE, heuristic, HTTP/2, HTTP-over-TLS, and unwalked tunnels are counted. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-prove-one-segment-http-host.md`)
- v1 reads every capture sequentially; classic pcap is not split across cores. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-read-every-capture-sequentially.md`)
- SSTP_DUPLEX_POST plus 200 in the same TCP segment switches leftover to an unwalked tunnel. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-same-segment-sstp-200-leftover-is-a-tunnel.md`)
- TCP RST skips HTTP dissection, matching tshark 4.6.9, even when the payload is a complete GET. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-skip-http-dissection-on-tcp-rst.md`)
- A 2xx to SSTP_DUPLEX_POST or a 101 with Upgrade whose headers are complete switches leftover Hosts to an unwalked tunnel, even with no body or Transfer-Encoding. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-sstp-2xx-and-101-upgrade-skip-body-desegment.md`)
- A TCP SYN still sets HTTP nxtseq to seq+1 when RST is set; RST payload is not HTTP and does not add its length. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-syn-rst-still-sets-http-nxtseq-to-seq-1.md`)
- A TCP SYN payload sets HTTP nxtseq to seq plus length plus one; FIN without SYN does not. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-tcp-nxtseq-after-syn-is-seq-plus-payload.md`)
- A jumbo option whose 2 + opt_len overruns the captured payload is truncated like PadN. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-truncate-jumbo-hop-dest-when-2-opt-len-overruns.md`)
- An Unproved prefix-extend suffix marks that TCP direction so the next in-order payload is counted continuation. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-02-unproved-http-suffix-marks-that-tcp-direction.md`)
- A complete HTTP header line with no colon is counted instead of treating leftover as Continuation. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-03-count-a-no-colon-http-header-line.md`)
- v1 http.host counts a no-colon header line, leftover NOTIFY, unreadable Content-Length, and a 1xx/204/304 that carries Content-Length. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-03-count-http-host-quirks-instead-of-proving-them.md`)
- A no-colon HTTP payload is counted even when a later Content-Length or chunked body is present. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-03-count-later-content-length-after-a-no-colon-line.md`)
- NOTIFY, SUBSCRIBE, and UNSUBSCRIBE payloads are counted instead of consuming leftover as notification body. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-03-count-leftover-notify-instead-of-treating-it-as.md`)
- A Content-Length that is not SP/HT digits is unreadable and the HTTP message is counted. (`.ax/decisions/2026-11-03-unprove-an-unreadable-http-content-length.md`)
